answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake that is slashed on fraud, like carving a claim into basalt: creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive because every identity locks real funds. Reputation then accrues only through verified work over time, so a newcomer cannot reach the summit of trust by spawning clones. A lightweight pigment-style fingerprint, a hash of hardware, payment, and behavior history, makes duplicate identities visible, letting peers reject copies before they can vote or earn.
